facts.statement: You built a Python application that used OpenAI GPT-4o-mini (temperature 0) to classify free-text veterinary radiology reports for 52 diagnostic conditions across three datasets (canine thorax, feline thorax, canine abdomen), scoring each condition in its own call with nine shared rules and JSON-configurable prompts.
You hand-scored 150 reports into a gold standard of 2,600 condition-level labels, and validated the model outputs against it.
You produced per-condition confusion matrices (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) in Vetology's output template.

You showed that accuracy was misleading under class imbalance because positives were only 4% to 10% of labels, so always answering "normal" would score 90% to 96%, and you reported per-condition sensitivity and specificity instead, using an offline keyword baseline to show accuracy overstated performance.
You found that legacy radiologist labels disagreed with the gold standard in about 40% of canine thorax cells.
You recommended a radiologist review of the gold standard and fixes for class imbalance and negative bias before the next evaluation, and presented the methodology and results to the Vetology team.

You rebuilt the original 231-line script with Claude Code into a modular package with unit tests, eight-worker concurrency, a response cache, and credentials moved from code to environment variables, and documented how manual coding compared with AI-assisted development.
You shipped the codebase to GitHub with controls that keep client data and credentials out of the repository.
